q: The part of the universe which we can see is termed the _____ universe.
e: The part of the universe which we can see is termed the visible universe. The physics in this sentence is built around visible involving termed.

q: The part of the universe we can see is determined by the _____ of the universe.
e: The part of the universe we can see is determined by the age of the universe. The physics in this sentence is built around age.

q: Among the objects studied in astrophysics are galaxies, stars, planets, exoplanets, the interstellar medium, and the cosmic _____ background.
e: Among the objects studied in astrophysics are galaxies, stars, planets, exoplanets, the interstellar medium, and the cosmic microwave background. The physics in this sentence is built around microwave.

q: The Earth is part of the solar system that contains _____ planets and the Sun.
e: The Earth is part of the solar system that contains eight planets and the Sun. The physics in this sentence is built around eight.

q: The closest star to our own is called _____.
e: The closest star to our own is called Proxima Centauri. Proxima Centauri names the closest star to our own.

q: Our group of galaxies is labeled the _____ Group and contains about 30 galaxies.
e: Our group of galaxies is labeled the Local Group and contains about 30 galaxies. The physics in this sentence is built around Local.

q: The main force holding all of these systems together is _____.
e: The main force holding all of these systems together is gravity. The physics in this sentence is built around gravity involving these.

q: An Astronomical Unit (AU) is the mean distance between the Earth and the _____.
e: An Astronomical Unit (AU) is the mean distance between the Earth and the Mars. The physics in this sentence is built around Mars.

q: A light year (ly) is the distance travelled by light in a _____ in one year.
e: A light year (ly) is the distance travelled by light in a vacuum in one year. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: One parsec (pc) is the distance to a star that subtends an angle of _____ at an arc length of 1 AU.
e: One parsec (pc) is the distance to a star that subtends an angle of 1 arc sec at an arc length of 1 AU. The physics in this sentence is built around 1 arc sec.

q: The theory that the universe must have originated at a single point of infinite density and finite time then began to expand is known as the _____ theory.
e: The theory that the universe must have originated at a single point of infinite density and finite time then began to expand is known as the Big Bang theory. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: After the initial expansion, the universe cooled sufficiently to allow the formation of _____ particles, and later simple atoms.
e: After the initial expansion, the universe cooled sufficiently to allow the formation of subatomic particles, and later simple atoms. The physics in this sentence is built around subatomic.

q: Giant clouds of primordial elements later coalesced through _____ to form stars and galaxies.
e: Giant clouds of primordial elements later coalesced through gravity to form stars and galaxies. The physics in this sentence is built around gravity.

q: The contents of the visible universe include ordinary matter (4.9%), dark matter (23%), and _____ (72%).
e: The contents of the visible universe include ordinary matter (4.9%), dark matter (23%), and dark energy (72%). Dark energy here means the capacity to do work. Ordinary matter: anything that has mass and occupies space.

q: The density of total energy in the visible universe is equivalent to _____ protons per cubic meter of space.
e: The density of total energy in the visible universe is equivalent to 6 protons per cubic meter of space. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.
